ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a solenoid, with the coil wound around a dashed central axis labeled "Axis of solenoid". Red arrows indicate the direction of the current in the wire, and the currents are all labeled I. Reasoning: The magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid satisfies B = μ0 n I, where μ0 is the medium constant and n is the number of turns per unit length. If the solenoid structure and medium are fixed, then B is directly proportional to the current I. Therefore, the magnetic field inside the solenoid is directly proportional to I.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as an ideal solenoid: a coil wound around a central dashed axis, with red arrows labeled I showing the same current flowing through the wire. Read the question asking what quantity the magnetic field inside an ideal solenoid is proportional to. Apply the standard ideal-solenoid relation B = μ0 n I, where n is turns per unit length and μ0 is constant for a given medium. Since the diagram labels the relevant varying electrical quantity as I, conclude that the inside magnetic field is proportional to I.
